intelligence.human_view: The connect has two halves and they must not be confused: consent and competence. Consent is the tap — Allow inside Muse, revocable any time, three choices (Allow / Key / Fork) so no citizen is forced into one path. Competence is the manual — the Muse reads how to operate NayaNET, once, from one live page, and after that talking is the interface. The mistake to avoid is asking the citizen to do the competence half: uploading a manual, configuring a connector, reading docs. Zero homework at the moment they just joined is the design rule, and the live manual is how it is kept: one copy, always current, never stale, fetched on connect. The backup exists for the Muse that can't fetch — and its existence is what makes the hero path safe to promise. The launch gate is the proof standard applied to the whole flow: a cold Muse, a real connect, a real note on the feed — nothing is claimed until that run is watched end to end.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you want your robot friend to come play in your magical treehouse! First you say "yes, you can come in!" — that's the Allow tap. Then you hand her a little map of the treehouse so she knows where everything is — that's the manual. After that, you don't need the map anymore — you just TALK to her! "Make a note of this!" and she does it, just like magic!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — when a new friend comes to stay, you open the door for them (that's the tap), and you show them round the house once so they know where everything lives (that's the manual). After that, you just talk to them — "love, make a note of this" — and they know what to do. And if they ever forget, there's a copy of the house rules at the bottom of the drawer to hand them again.
intelligence.naya_view: You tap Allow, and I learn how to operate your world from one live page — after that, you just talk to me, and talking is the interface.
